brief: 011 C round 5 step 1: production-finish mockups for v10 (signage hotbar)
tool: Codex CLI image tool via out/concepts/ui-011-r5/gen5.py (round 3/4 call with -i references); cost 0 per image; no Runware or other paid service
concurrency: 2 workers; 17 generations kept (4 portraits, 3 first-attempt panel sheets, 10 compact panel sheets); one batch killed by me and restarted with the compact prompt (c4, c5 never finished, not recorded)
supersedes: The first portrait pass used briefs/008/concepts/the-suborned-player-cell-concepts-2026-09-26.webp (not Sky's cell); dropped on Aster's correction, nothing from it is in any frame. Portraits come only from the four locked picks below.
method: Panel frames, verb plates, status pills and price chips are Codex images (physical-object renders on flat magenta, the portrait windows flat lime). I key them, fill the windows with the four portraits (cropped head and shoulders, inner shadow, hp pips), stretch the pill and chip with a repeating middle, engrave the verb glyphs on the buttons, and draw all text, numbers, over-head markers and the street layer in code (PIL, 3x supersampled) over the real Handover plates (briefs/011/ui/plates). The whole round is therefore art direction on real finish; the Unity build still needs the Step 2 sliceable kit.
plates: cafe-front-172430 (0:58 Pay on Inez), office-door-1730 (the take), service-lane-1730 (the fight). Cell, guards, rivals, cone, response car are drawn by scene.py (the plates carry none) and are identical under every direction. Latch's Unity screenshot and briefs/011/play/*.png were used as the reference for the layout only (they carry the text placeholders).
palette_check: CIEDE2000 against cone red #e03a2f, guard amber #f0a020, rival violet #8a4fd0. The Codex chrome and enamel carried warm and purple reflections: 0.9 to 4.7 % of panel pixels sat within dE 20 of a signal (worst r01 deco 4.7 %, r06 film 4.1 %, r09 sunburst 3.7 %). They are pulled toward neutral until every pixel clears dE 22 (fin2.guard_signals); after that 0.00 to 0.01 % in all ten. The selection turquoise #1cb9c6 is 42 to 58 from all three. Per-direction numbers are in coverage.
portrait_signal_check: scripts portsheet.py: at 66 px the Enforcer carries 1.7 % pixels within dE 12 of guard amber (lenses and gold panels) and 0.6 % violet-hue pixels (collar lining, sleeve trim); the Fixer's dress reads dark plum (0.0 % violet-hue); the Tech's cyan visor is dE 2 to 5 from the turquoise highlight. See s3.

generations.prompt: Character portrait pair for the roster of a polished video game, two square head-and-shoulders portraits side by side, each about 480 px square. The character is the young woman with the short dark undercut hair, the cream technical hooded jacket with the black harness straps and backpack straps, the gold accents and the small earpiece, exactly as in the attached reference image (same face, same hair, same costume, same colours and trim; do not redesign anything); a visitor from a nearby timeline, sharp and clean, matte technical fabrics. Both portraits show the same person, looking a little to the left of the viewer, alert. LEFT portrait, NORMAL: composed, the costume tidy. RIGHT portrait, HURT: after a scuffle, hair and clothes dishevelled, scuffs and dust on the costume, a bruise on the cheekbone or jaw, a tired pained expression, the head slightly bowed, any glasses or visor cracked or flickering; no blood and no red, only dust, grey scuffs and dark bruises. Framing for BOTH: chest-up, the head in the upper half and the same size in both, a slight turn, camera at eye level, the shoulders filling the lower third. Lighting for BOTH: one soft key light from the upper left and a cool seafoam rim light from behind on the right. Background of each portrait: a flat dim teal studio field #2c5a56, no gradient, no vignette, no scenery. Rendering: crisp, painterly-realistic game character art with clean edges, readable when shrunk to 72 px; no text, no frame, no border. Canvas rule: the space around and between the two portraits is one flat, perfectly even, solid magenta #ff00ff, at least 40 px wide; magenta never appears inside a portrait.
generations.use: portrait pair (normal + hurt) for the scout
